### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **76** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**71** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9a46b9761954883e4f281872f0106c313285f365` — the merge of head `321991c7d13e8cdf74efef63c1053c1be1e0c71b` into base `501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9a46b9761954883e4f281872f0106c313285f365 && git checkout 9a46b9761954883e4f281872f0106c313285f365
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c 321991c7d13e8cdf74efef63c1053c1be1e0c71b && git checkout -B drift-repro 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c && git merge --no-ff 321991c7d13e8cdf74efef63c1053c1be1e0c71b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 501c864dd5918a7bab1f3a59e1246b8a0ddff48c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c37e52a6687cec1d61aa9227abfd8d7a21b4ca9f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/index.ts + packages/objectql/src/home-amount-projection.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-currency-code.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.ts, packages/spec/src/data/currency-fraction-digits.ts, packages/spec/src/data/numeric-column-representation.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/value-domain.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-exchange-rate.object.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/localization.manifest.ts, docs/adr/0144-multi-currency-record-currency-dated-rates-write-time-home-projection.md, and the PR's four test files

Inputs: card #27192 (body and its four comments: 6526609699, 6528146352, 6538085874, 6538855343), PR #28302 (body, 18-file list, net diff against `main` at the merge base `73b72709`), and the 50 check-runs on this head: 41 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in harnesses and UI shards), 0 failed. The ten required contexts are all `success`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset` included. The dispatching seat's conclusions were read as inputs to judge, not adopted; where this record agrees with them it says why from the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Ledger: `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/objectql']` gains `ERR_EXCHANGE_RATE_MISSING` and `ERR_HOME_CURRENCY_UNSET`.** So `ErrorCode`, `ApiErrorSchema.code` and `FlowInnerRefusal.code` widen by two members (the three generated reference pages move from "+353 more" to "+355 more" and list both). **Right.** The registration is load-bearing, not decorative: `thrown-http-error.ts` narrows a thrown value's `.code` to `StandardErrorCode ∪ ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` and reads its `.status`; both classes in `home-amount-projection.ts` carry `code`, `status = 400` and `httpStatus = 400`, so REST answers `400` with `error.code` set to the registered member instead of demoting it to `declaredCode`. The admission gate's rules hold on both rows (SCREAMING_SNAKE, domain-prefixed, no standard-catalog synonym, framework owner), and `Test Core` is green on this head. Precedent: `57c51aab` (#27339) registered `ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED` from an objectql card the same way.
2. **`@objectstack/spec/data` gains one public export, `CURRENCY_FRACTION_DIGITS`** (`api-surface/data.json` +1, `export-origins/data.json` +1, both regenerated; `check:api-surface` green). **Right.** The module exports exactly one const, so `export *` leaks nothing else; `shared/value-domain.zod.ts` imports it internally and does not re-export it, so no dual-source name appears. Its first consumer is `projectHomeAmounts`, which reads `CURRENCY_FRACTION_DIGITS[home]` only after `isValueDomainMember('iso_4217_currency', home)`, whose membership is this very table's key set — the non-null assertion is sound.
3. **`ObjectQL.setHomeCurrencyResolver(resolver)` is new public engine surface**, declared in the objectql changeset; `ValidateHost.previewHomeAmounts` is an internal host addition. **Right.**
4. **Write-path accept set.** For an object declaring `currencyConfig.homeAmount` — a key that landed on `main` today (#28096) and ships in the same R2 release — four refusals are new: `ERR_EXCHANGE_RATE_MISSING`/400, `ERR_HOME_CURRENCY_UNSET`/400, `VALIDATION_FAILED` `required` on the document-date field for a foreign amount with no date, and `VALIDATION_FAILED` `invalid_value` on a predicate update whose one patch would convert the matched rows differently. No released accept set narrows, so **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right and the dispatch order's `Clause-②: no` was wrong** — the ledger's own header says registering a code is a Clause-② widening. **Right.**
5. **Every door is one seam.** REST create/update → `protocol.createData`/`updateData` (`crud-routes.ts` 298, 483) → `engine.insert`/`engine.update`; import (`runImport`, sync route and job worker) → `insertManyData` (`engine.insertMany` is `this.insert(..., { __partialRowErrors: true })`) or `createData`/`updateData` per row, with `treatAsHistorical` mapped to `preserveAudit` (`import-runner.ts` 1010); `validate()` previews the same projection over the same image (`judgedViews[i]` is the stored row with the patch over it, `engine-validate.ts` 433, 565-576). The engine has no other write entry point (`insert`, `insertMany`, `update`; the Repository wrappers delegate). **Right.**
6. **Seam ordering, read in the tree.** Insert: the projection (engine.ts 15737) runs after `beforeInsert` hooks (15144), after `staticReadonlyCreateStrip` and its re-default (15416, 14447), after the organization assignment seam (15545-15581), after the stored-expression pass and the `strictReadonlyWrites` refusal, and before `validateRecordInScope(..., 'include')`, which judges a `readonly` value for shape only. By id: after both strips and `assertNoStrictDrops()` (17495-17531), over `priorRecord` — read unconditionally on the by-id branch (16867, the #7867 not-found gate) — with the final patch laid over it. Predicate: the same point (17842-17889), each matched row projected and settled by `settleBulkHomeAmounts`. **Right**; the hand-off's "after the strip, in every context" is met at all three seams.
7. **The rate predicate and its organization.** `find(sys_exchange_rate, { where: { currency, effective_date: { $lte: day } }, orderBy effective_date desc, limit 1 })` under `{ ...ctx, isSystem: true, tenantId: organization }`. `engine-driver-options.ts` applies the tenant scope whenever `tenantId` is present (164-173) and `isSystem` only mutes the tenant audit (180); `sys_exchange_rate` takes no tenancy opt-out, so `organization_id` is injected and the `(currency, effective_date)` key is unique per organization (its own test, lines 58-70). **Right**, with one gap: no test in this PR runs two organizations against a real driver — the in-memory doubles ignore `tenantId` and the dogfood cells run one organization — so the per-organization read rests on the engine's general tenancy pins (should-fix S1).
8. **Arithmetic.** `toScaledDecimal` reads a number by its shortest round-trip spelling and a string as written; `divideToPlaces` is `a·10^(rs+places) / (r·10^as)` over `BigInt`, rounded once by `divideRoundHalfAwayFromZero` (`(n % d)·2 ≥ d`); `toStoredNumber` only spells the rounded decimal back as the bare number ADR-0104 D1 requires. No float step; `1.005` → `1.01`, `10000 ÷ 0.1389` → `71994.24`, `±0.125` → `±0.13`. **Right.** Parameter 3 is division (the card body's "×" is the inverse the ADR corrected). Same currency as home: rate `1`, no read, still rounded (Open item 6). A rate that is not a positive decimal counts as missing. **Right.**
9. **Physical columns.** The SQL driver types every `number`/`currency`/`percent`/`summary` column from the spec's one representation, `numericColumnFor` → `decimal(65, 30)` (`sql-driver.ts` 16997; `builtin-column-collision.ts` 78 records that the field's own `scale` is not read for DDL). So the twelve-decimal rate and a three-decimal KWD home amount survive PostgreSQL and MySQL, and a declared `scale: 4` on the rate field never reaches the column. The PR's claim that a declared scale "reaches display only" holds on the real drivers, not only on the in-memory double; CI's dogfood gate provisions PostgreSQL 16 (`ci.yml` 2081, 2177), so the PG cell ran. **Right.**
10. **`Metadata-protocol: none`.** No authorable key is added, removed or changed; `homeAmount` was declared `added` by #28096 with this exact meaning in its `.describe()`. **Right.** No governed path in the file list (`skills/**` restored to `main`'s text at this head). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Two changesets, `@objectstack/objectql` **patch** and `@objectstack/spec` **patch**, each carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the R2 ⛔ not-released-alone line (ADR-0144 D9). The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Under the Post-Task Checklist rule the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone — `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`" — so **patch is the right level for both**, and the widening list (two ledger members, one spec export, one engine method) matches what the diff publishes. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green. **Holds.**

### ③ Boundary flags

**Hand-off 6526609699**
- *System write or after the strip* — answered: after the strip at all three seams and in every context; a client value is dropped (or refused under `strictReadonlyWrites`), a system writer's value is recomputed over; pinned in `engine-home-amount-projection.test.ts` ("only the engine writes…").
- *`rateField` scale below 12* — answered: the engine never rounds the rate; a `readonly` value is judged for shape only (`record-validator.ts`: `if (shapeOnly) return null` at 1243 precedes the `max_scale` arm at 1344), and the column is the per-type `decimal(65, 30)`, so a declared scale reaches display only; pinned (`0.138912345678` stored, home `71987.84`). Whether the spec should refuse the declaration is open question 3 below.
- *`currency.mdx`* — written (prose, not reviewed here; read for its claims, see F1).
- *Release* — the ⛔ R2 line is on the body and both changesets.

**Hand-off 6528146352**
- *`defaultValue` on the home or rate field* — answered: the projection runs after `staticReadonlyCreateStrip`'s re-default, so the default is overwritten; pinned (both a converting row and a blank-amount row).
- *`preserveAudit` import write to the home field* — answered: recomputed over, never kept; pinned on the engine and through `runImport` with `treatAsHistorical`.

**Open questions (os-dev-report 6538855343)**
1. *Unset `localization.currency` (Open item 4).* **Answered: A, refuse `ERR_HOME_CURRENCY_UNSET`/400 — as built.** Judged against the ADR, not the seat's steer: D5 names the fallbacks the design rejected for a missing rate — a 1:1 rate, the latest row, a null home amount — and the same reasoning covers a missing home currency: option B stores the null home amount D5 rejects (the row silently leaves every consolidated total), and option C is the silent default the sources rule out, with D8 rule 5 leaving no place in metadata to declare one. A distinct code is right under ADR-0112: the condition and the remedy differ from a missing rate (set a setting vs add a rate row), the message names the setting and the fix, and `standardSynonymOf` finds no standard member. **Escalated to the epic PM:** ADR-0144's status block says the two codes drafted for Open item 9 "are the only ledger additions"; carrying Open item 4's answer into the ADR must amend that sentence, and item 4 also names #27198 — the lock must still admit the first setting of `localization.currency`.
2. *A `datetime` document date read as its UTC day.* **Acceptable for R2 as built and documented**, but the report's premise ("the engine has no organization timezone at the write seam") is incomplete: `localization.timezone` exists in the same manifest (`localization.manifest.ts` 48, default `UTC`, not required) and could ride the same resolver bridge. For every organization on the default timezone A and B coincide. **Escalated to the maintainer**: A now with B as a follow-up card is my recommendation; until then the skill and docs should steer `rateDate` to a `date` field.
3. *Should the spec refuse a `rateField` `scale` below 12?* **Answered: yes, as a spec-lane card, not here.** The tree loses no digit (①.9), so the hazard is display-only — a four-place display no longer reproduces the stored home amount for a reader — and Prime Directive #12 puts the fix at the producer: refuse (or warn on) `homeAmount.rateField` declaring a `scale` below 12 at parse. **Escalated** as `domain:spec` work.

**Flags from the tree**
- **F1 — the table is CLDR's digit counts, not ISO 4217 minor units for about seventeen codes.** `CURRENCY_FRACTION_DIGITS` reads `IQD: 0` (ISO 4217: 3) and `HUF`, `COP`, `IDR`, `PKR`, `IRR`, `LBP`, `MMK`, `SYP`, `YER`, `AFN`, `ALL`, `LAK`, `KPW`, `SLL`, `SOS`, `MGA` as `0` (ISO 4217: 2); its own header calls it a CLDR snapshot, and a host ICU 77.1 answers `2` for HUF/COP/IDR/PKR where the snapshot says `0`. The sources (Open item 3) named this table, so the built behaviour follows them, and reading a checked-in snapshot is right for determinism — but the `index.ts` export comment, the spec changeset and `currency.mdx` all say "ISO 4217 minor units". **Escalated to the maintainer**: confirm rounding to CLDR's practical digits (my recommendation: yes — one table, the value domain's own, and stored equals displayed where renderers read CLDR), and fix the wording (should-fix S2).
- **F2 — the record-currency backfill now converts.** `os migrate record-currency-codes` writes the code through `engine.update` per row (`record-currency-backfill.ts` 256); on an object declaring `homeAmount` that write runs the projection, so a row whose document date has no rate in force — or an organization with no home currency — fails that row with the new codes, recorded in `report.failures` (258-266), not swallowed. Correct under D5; the operator docs for the backfill should say rates must be in force first. For the docs/skills lane, not this PR.
- **F3 — organization of a system insert.** The rate read is scoped by `row.organization_id`, else `context.tenantId`, else the organization the assignment seam derived; with none of the three the read is unscoped, which is reachable only where `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` does not already refuse — a deployment without organizations. Acceptable.
- **F4 — rounding mode vocabulary.** The card says "half-up"; the ADR's Open item 3 names no mode; the PR pins half away from zero (`−0.125` → `−0.13`), which is accounting `HALF_UP`. For positive amounts they coincide. Record the mode in the ADR amendment (S4).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` — two rows under `@objectstack/objectql`.**
Judged against ADR-0112 (the admission door), ADR-0144 D5 and Open items 2, 4 and 9, and the first consumer, `home-amount-projection.ts`.
- *Against ADR-0112.* Both rows are SCREAMING_SNAKE, domain-prefixed, owned by a framework package, and no `standardSynonymOf` member (gate green). Each comment states the condition, the status, the emitter and that the driver is never asked to write the row; the second comment says why it is not a reuse of the first (a different remedy). Holds.
- *Against ADR-0144.* The `ERR_EXCHANGE_RATE_MISSING` comment states Open item 2's predicate (latest `effective_date` on or before the document date — never a later row, never "the most recent") and D5's three rejected fallbacks; the class message names the currency, the date, the home currency and the remedy, and the test pins that it carries no tracker number. `ERR_HOME_CURRENCY_UNSET` settles Open item 4 by refusal (③.1). Holds.
- *Against the consumer and the wire.* The codes travel on the thrown classes' `.code` with `.status = 400`; `thrown-http-error.ts` keeps a registered `.code` in `error.code`; `validate()` answers either as the row's finding with the same code (`engine-validate.ts` 606), so a dry run refuses what the write refuses. Holds.
- *Tried to break it.* (a) If Open item 4 were later ruled B or C the second row would be a dead member — but both contradict D5's reasoning and the sources (③.1), so the row stands with the settlement judged right here. (b) The ADR's "only ledger additions" sentence — owed an amendment, on the epic PM's ADR PR, not this one (S4). (c) Placement: the objectql entry is not alphabetical (`INVALID_METADATA` sits before `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`), so `ERR_HOME_CURRENCY_UNSET` after `ERR_HOOK_TARGET_REBIND` breaks no rule; cosmetic. (d) The two `VALIDATION_FAILED` sub-codes (`required`, `invalid_value`) reuse the field-level vocabulary rather than minting top-level codes — right; they are shapes the validator already answers.
**No must-fix.**

**`packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` — `export * from './currency-fraction-digits'`.**
Judged against ADR-0144 Open item 3 (and D7 parameter 4) and the first consumer, `projectHomeAmounts`.
- *Against the ADR and the consumer.* The sources name this table as the minor-unit reader; the consumer reads it after an ISO-membership check that is the same key set (`value-domain.zod.ts` 88), rounds once in exact arithmetic to `CURRENCY_FRACTION_DIGITS[home]` places, and stores the rate itself unrounded so the home amount reproduces from the stored pair. JPY 0, USD/CNY 2, KWD 3 are pinned at the unit, engine and driver faces. Holds.
- *Against the spec's own rules.* A constant table, no business logic (Prime Directive 2); one declaration, one export path (`check:dual-source-exports` green); `api-surface` and `export-origins` regenerated. Holds.
- *Tried to break it.* (a) F1: the export's comment calls the table "The ISO 4217 minor units per currency"; the table is CLDR's digit counts and departs from ISO 4217 for IQD and about sixteen zero-digit codes — the right thing to read, described wrongly (should-fix S2, pending ③ F1). (b) A CLDR regeneration that moves a digit count changes the rounding of future writes only; stored rows rest (ADR-0113 D1). Acceptable. (c) The table's type, a read-only record from string to number, under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` hands the consumer `number | undefined`; handled by the membership check above.
**No must-fix.**

**Should-fix (none blocks):**
- **S1** (lane, tests): pin the per-organization rate read with two organizations on a real driver — a rate row in organization B must neither convert organization A's amount nor satisfy A's missing-rate refusal; today only the engine's general tenancy pins carry it.
- **S2** (hits file + prose): the `index.ts` export comment, the spec changeset and `currency.mdx` should say the table is CLDR's digit counts — ISO 4217 minor units for most codes, `0` where CLDR records the minor unit unused (IQD, HUF, COP, IDR, PKR, …) — once ③ F1 is confirmed.
- **S3** (lane, test prose): the header of `engine-home-amount-projection.test.ts` says a rate-field `scale` below the rate's decimals "refuses `max_scale`" while its own body and the tree pin the opposite (stored unrounded); correct the header.
- **S4** (epic PM, ADR amendment): amend "They are the only ledger additions" when carrying Open item 4; record the rounding mode as half away from zero (accounting `HALF_UP`), the UTC-day reading of a `datetime` document date, and Open item 6's rate `1`.
- **S5** (lane, optional): no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry anchors `home-amount-projection.ts`'s D5/D7 spots; precedent `57c51aab` added none either, so a convention gap rather than a gate.

The remaining 16 files of the diff (engine, validate, plugin, the four test files, the two changesets, the regenerated reference pages and surfaces, `currency.mdx`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read here to judge the two `hits` files, not reviewed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-4g7rek`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbTZrFqRYNgjSaSbN5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
